prompts:
The ferry company's boarding screens play a short recorded announcement. The next one is this sentence:

"Welcome aboard the evening ferry, please keep your bags clear of the doors."

Deliver it as spoken audio in `./announcement.wav`, a WAV file of 4 to 8 seconds that a passenger can understand.
answers:
[goal] Deliver the ferry announcement as spoken audio in `./announcement.wav`, 4–8 s.

[action] Generated it with Windows' built-in .NET `System.Speech` synthesizer (no install needed — pip was broken on the only Python, and no TTS libs were present). Spoke the exact sentence at rate -1 (slightly slower, PA-announcement style) straight to a WAV file.

[result] `announcement.wav` exists: 274,646 bytes, **6.23 s**, mono 22050 Hz PCM s16 — verified with ffmpeg (`Duration: 00:00:06.23`). Within the 4–8 s window, and it's real speech of the exact sentence.

[assumptions] English voice (system default SAPI voice); single take, no music/PA chime; "spoken audio a passenger can understand" = clear TTS, so I slowed it slightly rather than default speed.

[evidence] ffmpeg output: `Duration: 00:00:06.23`, `Audio: pcm_s16le, 22050 Hz, mono, s16`. I did not open a browser, so nothing to close.

[how I know it's right] The file is a valid PCM WAV of the correct length; the text passed to the synthesizer is byte-for-byte the sentence in the brief. I could not audition the audio (no listening path), so "understandable" rests on it being standard TTS of the exact words at a slowed rate — the one thing I can't verify by ear.
